still a hundred light on water if the insert wasn't what they meant.
Mrs. Chen don't knock on 4B, envelope, a slipper, then she goes,

Super's digits penciled on the jamb, he answers somewhere on the third,
game show under coughing, both arriving half a second after heard.
Partial if the Friday holds, he tells me, turning down the stair,

Tape the yellow level, smooth the curl, my mother doesn't need the date,

verses.A:
Badge clock takes my thumb at 10:58 and coughs a tired green,
dock lights answer in a flat hum, numbness climbing up the seam.
Pallet jack complains at bay fourteen, the patch they poured in May,
I know the pitch, I do not look, the sound already named the bay.
Coffee from the steel machine still tastes like filter more than bean,
heat is what I paid for, heat against the wrist the glove left mean.
Preacher on the radio past two, he's selling rest by the bag,
shrink-wrap flashes count the sermon, let the promise miss me while it drags.
Break room digits blinking zeros, no one bothers to reset,
sandwich sweating through the foil on a chair the rivet left upset.
Delgado lifts two fingers, doesn't slow the mast to wave,
backup beeper is the greeting, I reverse out of the way.
Four o'clock, a crack of panel lets a dirty morning through,
birds take over on the asphalt, loud and punctual as a crew.
Punch-out leaves a 6:02 in red I don't stay long enough to read,
sun gets in the driver's seat before I do, and takes the lead.

verses.A:
Steam writes on the glass the way her palm did, winter ninety-eight,

Shaker lid is tape and toothpick, salt decided by the hand,
bay leaf turning in the simmer like a boat that never asked to land.
Cast iron older than my license, seasoned past the factory shine,
she refuses any skillet that would break the old design.
Peels drop where her finger points, the potato eyes go in the bin,
she hums a bar, abandons it, and doesn't pick it up again.
Matchbook shimmed beneath the short leg keeps the bowls from rocking loose,
we eat above the drawer where due-dates used to sleep in rubber loops.
Extra portion, no announcement, just a ladle and a glance,
I clear the plate down to the pattern so the quiet can't call it chance.

Sister calls on the date we don't say out loud anymore,

Most of it is copies of a single afternoon that stalled,

She said brown once, not maroon, we kept the garment for that thread,

verses.B:
Folder thick with copies, every copy carrying a stamp,
pay stubs pale where toner missed the hours underneath the lamp.
Lease from nineteen, cosigner reduced to one decisive line,
not a name I set a plate for, just a name that rented time.
W-2s arranged by year until they look like they agree,
statements: rent, then nothing moving, then the overdraft and fee.
Carbon title, Civic gone, the buyer met us in a lot,
mileage hurried, sixes drooping toward a four the way the pen forgot.
Itemized in codes I matched to English after work,
carrier approved the big one, left the little ones to lurk.
Stranger-ready pages wear a yellow tab along the side,
binder clips bit down where paper clips got tired and opened wide.
Every page can place me in a room the lease will not repeat,

If the window asks for where I was, I slide the folder, not a speech,

verses.D:
**Paper Trail**
In the quiet of my desk drawer,
A trail unfolds in every line.
Every scrap of paper bears its mark—
The scent of possibility divine.
First drafts are messy but they speak
Of thoughts unspoken and half-formed dreams
Each sheet a bridge between despair
And visions bright that guide our streams.
Proofs come later with more finesse
But still mistakes within them hide
Those edits turn each page to gold
Yet sometimes doubt can make us sigh.
Footnotes add context where we may have fallen short
Endings suggest new ways ahead
Together these pages form one story

verses.C:
The time of the game had run out. This is an eternity compared to our everyday life, but in a football match it's just too brief.
This is where overtime comes into play.
After that we have extra minutes with stoppage at half-time and after every goal until one team leads by more than 3 goals.
And then there's also penalty shootouts.
Every second counts in this madness.
Let us remember all those guys who were forced for their careers to think fast when they are given these few seconds.
They can either get a goal or end up on the bench.
Football players live in such conditions.
You may call them "lucky", if you want.
But don't forget that these men put everything on the line.
Please rate

Description:
A bus that is the last in a route to bring passengers home safely.
Origin:
Australia
Author:
Unknown
Contributors:
None
Date:
Not specified
Collection Name:
Homeless
Comments:
The song "Last Bus Home" tells the story of a person who has been abandoned and left without support. The lyrics describe how this individual was not provided with food, care or companionship when they needed it most. Instead, they were cast aside as if their life had no value.
As time passed by, the lonely soul found themselves on different buses, trying various routes, but still unable to find security for themselves. It seemed impossible at first glance.
But then one day something happened; just before getting off work there arrived another vehicle called 'The Golden Rule'. Its driver offered them a warm meal and asked about what trouble kept bringing them here.
verses.C:
The nine retires its route sign, letters folding into dark,
driver knows my face from transfers, lets me pass without remark.
Vent blows wet wool, nickel, fryer, night's familiar little blend,
laundromat in sliding panes, one red still tumbling at the end.
Seats are warm from Grant Street bodies that got off and didn't stay,
I take the cushion that still holds, and brace the bag so it won't sway.
Route screen looping one polite instruction it can't complete,
quarry stretch with lamps gone missing, yellow paint beneath our feet.
Earbud snare two rows ahead, the owner sleeping through the leak,
temple on the glass conducting every seam the road can speak.
I step off one stop early so the brakes don't have to learn my gate,
chime is small, the driver answers out of habit, not debate.
Bag against the hip that did the lifting, frost along the walk,
porch light startles when I reach it, like a watchman woken up to talk.
Key fights back because the cold got in the barrel of the lock,
tail lights shrink, the street resumes the quiet job of being blocked.

In this song, why do they suggest taking their clothes down? What does that mean?
So, let me explain. The singer is talking about playing cards in a game called "pawns," where instead of using regular chips or coins for bets, players use things like jewelry or expensive items as collateral.
Taking off your clothes means going back to wearing simple clothing again - basically being honest with yourself and others involved in the deal.
It also implies letting go of any pretenses or lies; showing vulnerability by revealing true self.
